exercise_description: While working on a branch, I initiated a merge.
I am presented with merge prompt screen, but now I wish to abort the operation.
hints: Read the instructions on the merge prompt screen carefully.
What happens if you close the terminal window without any changes ?
What happens if you delete the commit message ?

checks.name: Check commit message
explanation: Check that the user has closed the editor with the commit message prompt.

checks.name: Check git history
explanation: Check the git history for presence of git merge commits.
checks.command: test -z "$(git lg | grep "Merge branch 'feat' - Git Master (HEAD -> main)")"

exercise_description: I worked on a feature and I wanted to rebase my branch upon main,
But instead I accidentally did a merge.
I want to the merge and have a linear history.
hints: Use 'git lg' to check the history of the commits.
Be careful not to loose any files, or any commits
Git reflog is a trap
Try resetting your HEAD~1

checks.name: Check git history
explanation: Check the git history for presence of git merge commits.

checks.name: Check files
explanation: Check that are all files are present in the working tree.
checks.command: for f in file1.txt file2.txt file3.txt; do [ -f "$f" ] || { echo "Missing $f"; exit 1; }; done

checks.name: Check commits
explanation: Check all three commits are present 'first', 'second' and 'third'

exercise_description: I edited the text1.txt file
I want to rebase my feat branch onto main
But another user edited the same file on main
hints: When conflicts occur during rebase, git will pause and show you the conflicted files.
Edit the conflicted files to resolve merge conflicts manually.
After resolving conflicts, use 'git add' to mark files as resolved.
Continue the rebase process with 'git rebase --continue'.
If you want to abort the rebase, use 'git rebase --abort'.

checks.name: Check commit history
explanation: After rebasing all commits should be present in the history
checks.command: for s in "I too edited file1" "edited file1"; do git log --pretty=%s | grep -Fxq "$s" || { echo "Missing commit: $s"; exit 1; }; done

checks.name: Check file content
explanation: The file content should contain both the text from the first and second commits

exercise_description: I accidentally committed my password to the repo
I want to completely remove any mention of my password from the history
hints: Use 'git lg' to view the commit history
On what branches is it present ?
How do you remove the commit from both local and remote branch ?
How about the git objects ?
git-filter-repo --sensitive-data-removal --replace-text password.txt --force
git push --force --mirror origin

checks.name: Check git history for password
checks.command: test $(git rev-list --objects --all | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -n1 git cat-file -p | grep 'pa$$word' -c) -eq 0
explanation: The user should have successfully removed the commit from the history. Check the git objects to ensure that password is no longer present in git's internals.

checks.name: Check git history
explanation: Make sure other commits are not lost
checks.command: git lg | grep -q "some content - Git Master"

exercise_description: A colleague works on another repository that is not related to mine and have pushed a commit called 'other commit'.
I want to get the content of their commit on my repo.
I added the second repository as a remote and pulled
And I receive the following error when trying merge: fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories
hints: Next hint will reveal the solution
Use git merge --allow-unrelated-histories

checks.name: Check worktree files
explanation: The worktree should contain a file called 'file_other.txt' from the other remote.

checks.name: Check git history
explanation: The git history should contain a commit called 'other commit' from the other remote.
checks.command: git lg | grep -q "other commit - Git Master"

exercise_description: I try to create a branch called "feat/my_feat"
But when I try to push it to the remote, it results in an error
! [remote rejected] feat/mine -> feat/mine (failed to update ref)

checks.name: Check the local branch has been pushed to remote.
explanation: Verify that the user has successfully resolved the error and pushed the branch to the remote.

hints: Is your local up-to date ?
Do a git fetch, and then git branch -a
Is there anything unusual in the branch name that came from the remote ?
Since git refs are stored as files in directory structure, having a ref called 'feat' will cause problems when we want to create a branch called 'feat/<name>'.
One solution would be to rename your local branch to feature/mine

exercise_description: I worked on a feature
And I had to quickly change a branch so I performed a "WIP" commit at one point.
I want to clean this WIP commit before opening my merge request.
hints: Be careful, git reset HEAD~2 is not a good idea.
How about interactive rebase ?
git rebase -i HEAD~3, then prefix the commit with s to squash it.
Don't forget to push --force your branch.

checks.name: Check git history
explanation: Check the git history for presence of the WIP commit.

checks.name: Check worktree files
explanation: Check that the file related to the WIP commit has not been lost.

exercise_description: I did a wrong checkout
Now my HEAD is in a detached state
I want to attach my HEAD to a branch so that further commits are kept
hints: Use 'git status' to see the 'detached HEAD' notice.
Simply reattach to an existing branch: git checkout main.
Avoid committing while detached or you may lose the commit reference.

checks.name: HEAD is attached to a branch
explanation: Ensure HEAD points to a branch, not a detached state.

checks.name: No commits lost
explanation: Verify that the original 'second commit' still exists in the repository graph.

exercise_description: I fixed two bugs that required editing the same file.
I want to split it into two different commits.
However, when I perform 'git add -p' the two changes are added together.
hints: Use 'git add -p' to interactively stage changes.
If both lines show up as a single hunk, press 'e' to edit the patch.
In the patch editor remove the lines you don't want to stage yet, keep context lines intact, then save and exit.
Commit the staged part, then stage and commit the remaining change.

checks.name: Both changes present in file
explanation: Ensure both lines are present in the working tree after splitting into commits.
checks.command: grep -Fxq 'This line should be in first commit' file1.txt && grep -Fxq 'This line should be in a second commit' file1.txt

checks.name: Two separate commits for the changes
explanation: Verify that each of the last two commits adds exactly one of the lines (order does not matter).
checks.command: ( git show -U0 HEAD -- file1.txt | grep -Fq "+This line should be in first commit" && git show -U0 HEAD~1 -- file1.txt | grep -Fq "+This line should be in a second commit" ) || ( git show -U0 HEAD -- file1.txt | grep -Fq "+This line should be in a second commit" && git show -U0 HEAD~1 -- file1.txt | grep -Fq "+This line should be in first commit" )

checks.name: Initial commit preserved
explanation: Ensure the original 'initial commit' still exists behind the two new commits.

exercise_description: I did multiple commits but forgot to include a file in the previous (not last) commit.
I want to amend that earlier commit to include the missing file without changing later commits.
hints: Use interactive rebase to edit a non-last commit: git rebase -i HEAD~2.
Change 'pick' to 'edit' for the commit you want to modify.
Stage the missing file: git add file_to_add_to_second_commit, then git commit --amend --no-edit.
Continue the rebase: git rebase --continue.
If already pushed, update the remote with git push --force-with-lease.

checks.name: Edited commit includes the file
explanation: Verify that the commit with subject 'second' now includes 'file_to_add_to_second_commit'.
checks.command: second=$(git log --pretty=%H:%s | awk -F: '$2=="second"{print $1; exit}'); test -n "$second" && git show --pretty= --name-only "$second" | grep -qx "file_to_add_to_second_commit"

checks.name: Commit order preserved
explanation: Ensure the last two commit subjects remain 'third' then 'second'.

checks.name: Worktree contains the file
explanation: The file added to the 'second' commit should also exist in the current working tree.

exercise_description: I did some wrong operation
Now I see the commits of my colleague as part of my PR
I want to keep only my changes on this branch
hints: Use 'git lg' to inspect history and identify foreign commits.
Those commits likely came from an accidental merge.
You can rewrite history to drop them: interactive rebase or reset and cherry-pick your own commit(s).
After rewriting, push with --force-with-lease to update the remote.

checks.name: No merge commit present
explanation: Ensure the branch no longer contains a merge commit that brought in foreign history.

checks.name: Foreign commits removed
explanation: Commits from the other branch '(other branch)' should not be in current branch history.

checks.name: My work preserved
explanation: Your own commit and file should remain after cleanup.
checks.command: git lg | grep -q 'first commit' && test -f file3.txt

exercise_title: Get Most Recent Code from Main
exercise_description: I am working on a feature branch.
A colleague pushed new commits to the main branch.
I want to get the latest changes from main onto my branch and then merge to main.
I want to keep the history linear and avoid unnecessary merge commits.
hints: Use 'git lg' to inspect both your branch and main.
Fetch remote updates so 'origin/main' points to the newest commit.
Try rebasing your branch onto 'origin/main' to keep history linear.
Verify that files introduced on main exist on your branch afterward.

checks.name: On the feature branch
explanation: Ensure the current branch is 'feat' as prepared by the script.

checks.name: Main commits are present
explanation: Commits from 'main' (subjects 'second commit' and 'third commit') should be in your branch history after syncing.
checks.command: git log --pretty=%s | grep -Fxq 'second commit' && git log --pretty=%s | grep -Fxq 'third commit'

checks.name: Files from main exist
explanation: Files added on 'main' should exist in the working tree with expected content.
checks.command: test -f file2.txt && test -f file3.txt && grep -qx 'content2' file2.txt && grep -qx 'content3' file3.txt

exercise_description: I want git to ignore the "dist" directories, but for some reason it is not working.
hints: Use a .gitignore file at the repository root to ignore build artifacts.
Add a rule that covers both top-level 'dist/' and nested 'src/dist/'.
Files already tracked won't be ignored automatically; remove them from the index with 'git rm -r --cached dist src/dist'.
Commit the .gitignore and the removal from index; do not delete the files from disk.
Verify with 'git ls-files' or 'git status' that dist paths are no longer tracked and 'src/src.txt' is tracked.

checks.name: Dist paths are ignored
explanation: Ensure typical dist outputs are matched by ignore rules.
checks.command: git check-ignore -q dist/file1.txt && git check-ignore -q src/dist/file2.txt

checks.name: Dist paths are not tracked
explanation: Ensure no files under 'dist/' or 'src/dist/' remain in the index.

checks.name: File Content is not Deleted
explanation: Make sure local files are not deleted after ignoring them.

exercise_description: I forked a repository from a remote
Someone has pushed some new code to the original remote in branch main
I want to get the latest changes from the original remote
The second remote is located at file:///git/.git-repos/multiple_remotes_update_main-upstream.git
hints: Use 'git remote -v' to list remotes.
You can add the new remote with the git remote add command
You can then pull from the remote branch with git pull <remote2> main

checks.name: Check the remote
explanation: The second remote has been added.

checks.name: Check the worktree
explanation: Check that the worktree has been updated with the content from the new remote.

exercise_description: I finished working on my feature
And I want to merge my code to main
But I do not want to generate a merge commit
In order to keep history clean and linear

checks.name: No merge commits
explanation: There should be no merge commits in the commits history.

checks.name: Check the worktree
explanation: Both files from the feature branch should be present in the worktree

exercise_description: I have an untracked file called 'file2.txt' on branch 'feat'.
This file exists and is tracked on 'main'.
When I try to checkout 'main' I get an error about untracked files being overwritten.
hints: Use 'git status' to review untracked files blocking the switch.
Check which branch tracks 'file2.txt' and which doesn't.
Try stashing untracked files with 'git stash -u' before switching.
After switching to 'main', restore your work if needed with 'git stash pop'.

checks.name: On main branch
explanation: Ensure you successfully switched to 'main'.

checks.name: Tracked file from main present
explanation: The tracked 'file2.txt' version from main should exist with expected content.

checks.name: Commit present in history
explanation: Verify that 'second commit' from 'main' is in history after switching.

checks.name: Working tree is clean
explanation: Ensure no pending changes remain after resolving the checkout issue.

exercise_description: Me and a colleague worked on the same branch 'feat'.
They committed a change on the remote and I committed locally.
When I pulled, Git created a merge commit on my branch.
I want to keep the history linear and remove the accidental merge.
hints: Use 'git lg' to see the merge commit that pull created.

checks.name: No merge commits present
explanation: Ensure the branch history is linear (no merge commits).

checks.name: Both commits preserved
explanation: Verify both the colleague's and your 'first commit' exist (authors differ).
checks.command: git lg | grep -Fq 'first commit - Tim Who Eats Your Sandwich' && git lg | grep -Fq 'first commit - Git Master'

checks.name: On branch 'feat'
explanation: Confirm you are working on the expected branch.

checks.name: Worktree contains the file
explanation: Ensure 'file1.txt' exists after resolving history. Content may be from either commit.
checks.command: test -f file1.txt && ( grep -qx 'content 1' file1.txt || grep -qx 'content from colleague' file1.txt )

exercise_description: I am working on a feature and have not yet committed.
I need to quickly switch to 'main' to fix an urgent issue.
I want to keep my current work safe while switching.
hints: You can create a wip commit
Or use stash

checks.name: On main branch
explanation: Ensure you successfully switched to 'main'.

checks.name: Work files not present on main
explanation: Temporary work files should not remain in the working tree after switching.
checks.command: test ! -e work_file.txt && test ! -e src/f1.txt && test ! -e src/f2.txt && test ! -e src/f3.txt && test ! -e src/f4.txt

checks.name: Changes saved via stash or commit
explanation: Accept either approach: a stash exists, or 'feat' tracks the work files (WIP commit).
checks.command: test -n "$(git stash list)" || git ls-tree -r --name-only feat | grep -Eqx "work_file.txt|src/f1.txt"

checks.name: Working tree clean
explanation: Ensure no pending changes remain on 'main' after the switch.

exercise_description: I did a commit, but I want to add some files to it.
I want to push my code to the remote.
hints: Be careful not to

checks.name: Amended commit preserved
explanation: The last two commit subjects should be 'Redo this commit <--' and then 'first commit' (no extra commit created).
checks.command: test "$(git log --pretty=%s -n2 | paste -sd , -)" = "Redo this commit <--,first commit"

checks.name: File included in last commit
explanation: Ensure 'file_to_add.txt' is part of the amended last commit.

checks.name: Remote updated to HEAD
explanation: The remote 'origin/main' should point to the amended commit (requires force-with-lease).
checks.command: git fetch -q origin && test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$(git rev-parse origin/main)"

checks.name: Files present in worktree
explanation: Both 'file3.txt' and 'file_to_add.txt' should exist in the working tree.
checks.command: test -f file3.txt && test -f file_to_add.txt && grep -qx 'content3' file3.txt
